messages.subject: Spacing in multiple-select options
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to 'mimic' a table using a multiple select (selectInput(...,multiple=TRUE)) by inserting spaces and vertical bars so that the text in each row lines up. However, I run into the issue that when displayed, the options lose their spacing.

For example, if i have under selectInput('multiSelect','   A|   B',vec.out) with

vec.out = c(1,2,3)
names(vec.out)= c('   1|   2','  11|  22',' 111| 222')

and spaces such that the string is of length 4 to the left and to the right of the bar. The idea is that the multiple select will render such that it resembles a data frame with right justified columns df$A=c(1,11,111) and df$B=c(2,22,222). Unfortunately, the extra blank spaces for the first few rows are shortened to just 1 when the selectInput is rendered.

I've tried doing a gsub to replace all the spaces with   but then all the text is just rendered verbatim, i.e.

   A|   B
   1|   2
  11|  22
 111| 222

How should I go about this?
Thanks,
Ray

messages.author: 76cfff2ce20c1a35
messages.subject: Re: Spacing in multiple-select options
parts:
So I looked into the underlying code and it seems that the main issue is that somewhere in the selectInput function it escapes '&'s by replacing them with '&amp' string. It is necessary to 'unescape' by having as the last line of selectInput a gsub wrapper which re-replaces '&amps' with '&', i.e. instead of

tagList(controlLabel(inputId, label),selectTag) 

replace it with

gsub('&','&',tagList(shiny:::controlLabel(inputId, label), selectTag)).

TL;DR: To preserve spacing, replace all spaces with the nonbreakable space character '&nbsp', then in selectInput replace the final line of code with a gsub operation.

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: Spacing in multiple-select options
parts:
gsub('&','&') does not look good, even though it may work in this
particular case, since it may unescape characters that should have
been escaped, e.g. selectInput('foo', label='Foo&', choices=1:3)

Perhaps selectInput() should provide an additional argument "names"
which is names(choices) by default, and users can also provide
HTML("custom html names") so that the names will not be escaped -- the
preferred approach to preventing character strings from being escaped
is HTML(), but that does not apply to selectInput() at the moment. I
think you can file a feature request to
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues

Regards,
Yihui
